title: Sunny Watches the Milky Way | Bedtime Story
description: Sunny the Quokka finds a clearing on a perfect dark night and stares up at the Milky Way stretching like a river of stars from one end of the bush to the other. A magical bedtime story for toddlers from Sunny's Little Bedtime Stories.
narration:
Sunny had never seen the sky quite like this before.

She had found a wide clearing — the biggest she had ever come across — where the trees opened up and there was nothing between her and the entire sky.

And the sky was full.

Not just stars — though there were thousands of stars. But a whole band of light stretching from one end of the world to the other. Milky and soft and endlessly deep. A river of light made of more stars than Sunny could ever count in a hundred lifetimes.

She lay down in the middle of the clearing and put her paws behind her head.

The Milky Way stretched right over her, from east to west, as if someone had drawn a gentle brushstroke across the sky.

She tried to look at one part of it and found she could not — it was too big, too many, too beautiful to look at any single place. She could only look at all of it.

So she did.

She lay there and let the enormity of it wash over her. All those stars. All that light. All of it so far away, and yet the light reaching all the way down to touch her little golden face.

Somewhere in the bush a cricket sang.

Somewhere the creek flowed.

But mostly there was just the sky, enormous and soft.

And Sunny, small and warm and perfectly held.

Goodnight, Sunny. Goodnight, Milky Way. Goodnight, little one.
